title: Searching and Sorting
summary: Binary search, rotated arrays, intervals, search on the answer

guide.title: Order makes everything faster
points: Searching a sorted list of a million items takes 20 steps with binary search instead of a million.
Many hard questions become easy after sorting: merge intervals, meeting rooms, two pointers, duplicates.
Binary search on the answer ("smallest speed that finishes in time") is a favourite in product-company rounds.

guide.title: Where searching and sorting run
points: Databases keep sorted indexes (B-trees) so a lookup by roll number or order id is instant.
E-commerce sorts by price, rating and relevance; leaderboards sort by score.
git bisect binary-searches your commit history to find the commit that broke the build.
Calendars merge overlapping meetings; ride apps sort drivers by distance.

guide.title: Halve the search space
points: Binary search needs sorted data (or any yes/no condition that flips once).
Look at the middle: if it is too small, the answer is on the right; otherwise on the left. Each step halves the range: O(log n).
Sorting: use the built-in sort (O(n log n)); know how merge sort and quick sort work for interviews.

guide.title: Sort numbers and binary search
points: JavaScript sort() compares as text by default: always pass a comparator for numbers.

guide.title: Binary search on the answer
points: When the question asks for the smallest (or largest) value that works, and "works" stays true once it becomes true, binary search over the values.
Example: the smallest capacity that ships all packages in d days. Check a capacity in O(n); search capacities in O(log range).

guide.title: Sort first, then sweep
points: Merge intervals: sort by start; extend the last interval while the next one overlaps, otherwise start a new one.
Custom order: sort with a comparator (by end time, by length, by two keys).
Merge step of merge sort: two pointers on two sorted lists, take the smaller each time: O(n + m).

guide.title: What breaks search and sort code
points: JavaScript: [10, 9, 1].sort() gives [1, 10, 9]. Always sort numbers with (a, b) => a − b.
Endless loops in binary search: with lo < hi and lo = mid, the range may stop shrinking. Match the loop condition and updates.
(lo + hi) can overflow int in Java and C++; use lo + (hi − lo) / 2.
Binary search on unsorted data gives wrong answers silently.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Know lower bound (first ≥ x) and upper bound (first > x); most variants are one of these.
Rotated sorted array: one half around mid is always sorted; decide which side the target is on.
Quick select finds the k-th smallest in O(n) on average; counting sort is O(n + range) for small values.
Stable sort keeps equal items in their original order (merge sort, JavaScript and Java object sorts, Python sort).
Next step: Dynamic Programming.

problems.title: Binary search
problems.statement: nums is sorted with distinct values. Return the index of target or -1.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Keep lo and hi and look at the middle.

problems.title: Squares in sorted order
problems.statement: nums is sorted. Return the squares of all elements, also sorted.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: The biggest square is at one of the two ends.

problems.title: First and last position
problems.statement: nums is sorted and may repeat values. Return the first and last index of target, or "-1 -1".
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Binary search for the left border, and again for the right.

problems.title: Search in a rotated array
problems.statement: A sorted array of distinct values was rotated. Return the index of target or -1 in O(log n).
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Find which half is sorted and whether target is inside it.

problems.title: Merge intervals
problems.statement: Merge all overlapping intervals (touching ends overlap). Return them sorted by start, one per line.
inputFormat: intervals: a count k, then k lines of integers
problems.hint: Sort by start, then extend the last one or add a new one.

problems.title: Ship packages within D days
problems.statement: Packages are loaded in order. Return the smallest ship capacity that moves all of them within the given days.
inputFormat: weights: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Binary search the capacity between the heaviest package and the total.

problems.title: Median of two sorted arrays
problems.statement: Both arrays are sorted and not both empty. Return the median of all values (a .5 result prints as .5).
inputFormat: a: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
b: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Merging works; the O(log) way binary searches the split point of the smaller array.
